name: Qara Khitai (Western Liao)
summary: Founded by Khitan nobles who fled the fall of the Liao dynasty; under Yelü Dashi it defeated the Seljuks at Qatwan (1141) and ruled Central Asia until the Mongols took it in 1218.

location.value: Central Asia: the Chu and Ili valleys (today’s Kyrgyzstan and Kazakhstan), with power over the Tarim Basin and Transoxiana.

terrain.value: Steppe and mountain valleys of the Tian Shan, with irrigated oases.

climate.value: Dry continental: hot summers, cold winters.

resources.value: Horses and herds, irrigated farmland and the wealth of Silk Road trading cities.

disasters.value: Droughts and harsh winters on the steppe.

population.value: The Khitan ruling group was small (tens of thousands); the subject peoples numbered millions.

urbanisation.value: The capital Balasagun (Huzi Wo’erduo); rich vassal cities such as Samarkand, Bukhara and Kashgar.

disease.value: Epidemics and famines, especially in war.

migration.value: Khitans led by Yelü Dashi fled west after the Liao dynasty fell to the Jurchens (1124–25).

economicBase.value: Tribute from vassal states, herding, and taxes on oasis farming and trade.

tradeRoutes.value: Controlled the central Silk Road between China and the Islamic world.

wealth.value: Rich from the tribute of Silk Road cities.

moneyAndTax.value: Light taxes, reportedly about one dinar per household; vassals paid tribute; some Chinese-style coins were cast.

inequality.value: Rulers and military elites above farmers and herders.

keyRulers.value: Yelü Dashi (ruled 1124–43), the founder; Empress Xiao Tabuyan and Empress Yelü Pusuwan; Yelü Zhilugu, the last ruler (1178–1211).

succession.value: Within the Yelü family; two empresses ruled as regents or in their own right.

institutions.value: A Chinese-style court with officials, alongside local rulers who stayed in power as vassals.

stability.value: Stable for decades, but vassals rebelled in the 1200s and the Naiman prince Kuchlug seized power (1211).

eliteConflict.value: Vassals such as Khwarazm and the Kara-Khanids rebelled; Kuchlug usurped the throne.

armyAndTech.value: Disciplined cavalry organised in Chinese and steppe style.

majorWars.value: Battle of Qatwan on 9 September 1141, north of Samarkand.

territoryChange.value: Took control of the Kara-Khanids, Transoxiana, Khwarazm (as a tributary) and the Uyghur kingdom of Qocho.

alliancesRivals.value: Rivals of the Seljuks; later of Khwarazm; Kuchlug’s rule ended with the Mongol conquest.

scienceEducation.value: Chinese-style learning at court and Islamic learning in the vassal cities.

openness.value: Open to trade and tolerant of different religions.

communicationTransport.value: Horses and caravans on Silk Road routes.

religion.value: Buddhist rulers with Muslim, Christian, Manichaean and Buddhist subjects; Kuchlug later persecuted Muslims.

languageWriting.value: Khitan and Chinese at court; Persian, Arabic and Turkic among the subjects.

artsArchitecture.value: Little survives; Balasagun has Kara-Khanid and earlier remains.

socialStructure.value: A small Khitan ruling class above many Turkic, Persian and other peoples.

sharedIdentity.value: Loyalty to the Gurkhan (the ruler’s title) among the Khitan; subjects kept their own identities.

dailyLife.value: Herders lived in tents on the steppe; oasis people farmed and traded in the towns.

neighbours.value: Khwarazm, the Kara-Khanids, the Naimans and other Mongolic tribes, the Uyghurs and the Jin dynasty.

ideasReligions.value: Religious tolerance; the defeat of a Muslim sultan at Qatwan may have fed the European legend of Prester John.

riseSignals.value: Founded by Yelü Dashi, who proclaimed himself king in 1124 and took the titles Emperor and Gurkhan in 1132; capital Balasagun.

peakPeriod.value: After Qatwan (1141), when the Gurkhan was overlord of most of Central Asia.

declineSignals.value: Khwarazm rebelled and the Naiman prince Kuchlug seized power (1211).

outcome.value: The Naimans under Kuchlug usurped the empire in 1211; the Mongol conquest of 1218 ended it (the lead gives 1124–1218).

overallCertainty.value: Main events are known from chronicles; population figures are estimates.
